prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1092; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recording is for claim review purposes. Can you please state your full name for the record?

A: Yes, I'm the claimant. You have my name on file already, so I'll just say I'm the driver of the vehicle that was rear-ended.

Q: Understood. Can you walk me through what happened at the time of the collision?

A: I was stopped at a light on a main road in Pearland, Texas, waiting for the signal to change. I had come to a complete stop when I felt a hard impact from behind. My head snapped back and then forward, and my seatbelt locked up.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?

A: Not really. I checked my mirror a moment before, but the car behind me was a bit further back. I didn't have time to react after that.

Q: Were you able to get out of your vehicle at the scene?

A: Yes, I got out, but I felt dizzy and stiff. The other driver was apologetic and we exchanged information. A police officer came out and filed a report.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the collision?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that same day and was later referred to a physical therapist. I have neck pain that radiates into my shoulders, and I get headaches, mostly in the afternoon. Turning my head to check blind spots is painful.

Q: Are you still experiencing those symptoms now?

A: Yes, they're improving slowly, but I still have stiffness in the morning and I've had to cut back on driving longer distances.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I'm willing to provide my medical records and the report number from the officer.

Q: Thank you for your cooperation. This concludes the recorded statement.
